statement: A local authority has the power to take legal action against an unauthorized construction that may be deemed to obstruct a private individual's interest.
supporting_quote: the powers still, remain in the local authorities to take legal action against the unauthorized constructions erected within its purview that may, be deemed to be obstructing the private individual’s interest

statement: A party cannot directly dispute the final scheme of Partition if they are not a party to the Partition action.
supporting_quote: the remedy of restitutio in integrum can only be availed of by one who is actually a party to the contract or legal proceeding in respect of which restitution is desired.

statement: Before dismissing a partition action for non-prosecution, the court must compel the parties to bring the action to a termination.
supporting_quote: In terms of the provisions of section 70 of the Partition Law, before dismissing a partition action for non-prosecution, the court has to compel the parties to bring the action to a termination.

statement: A party cannot seek relief under Restitutio-in-Integrum if they have an alternative remedy equally effectual open to them.
supporting_quote: Restitutio-in-Integrum is not granted in Ceylon if the applicant has any other remedy equally effectual opened to him.

statement: A person who has divested themselves of all right, title, and interest in a property prior to the institution of a partition action is not a necessary party to the action.
supporting_quote: The petitioner is neither a co-owner of the subject property nor a person presently possessing any. The petitioner has no right, share or interest in the corpus of the Partition Action. The material placed before Court indicates that the petitioner had divested himself of all right, title, and interest in the property prior to the institution of the action.

statement: When a company's name is struck off, the property of the company generally vests in the State, but if the company held the property on trust for another person, the property may vest in that person.
supporting_quote: When the name of the company is struck off, the property of the company generally vests in the State. However, as the petitioner claims, the question of whether he became the owner of the property should be decided at the trial.

statement: Where the corpus to be partitioned has not been sufficiently identified either by means of the stated boundaries or by extent, an appeal court can interfere with an interlocutory decree by way of revision or restitutio in integrum where a miscarriage of justice has occurred.
supporting_quote: In this case the corpus to be partitioned had not been sufficiently identified either by means of the stated boundaries or by extent and the land of the petitioner appeared to be included in the corpus. Therefore, there has been a miscarriage of justice.

statement: A mistake on the part of the Learned Additional District Judge resulted in wiping out the petitioner's entitlement to the land and thereby causing prejudice to the petitioner's substantial rights.
supporting_quote: A mistake on the part of the Learned Additional District Judge resulted in wiping out the petitioner's entitlement to the land and thereby causing prejudice to the petitioner's substantial rights.

statement: The powers of revision and restitutio in integrum have survived all the legislation that has been enacted up to date.
supporting_quote: The powers of revision and restitutio in integrum have survived all the legislation that has been enacted up to date.

statement: A person affected by void proceedings can apply to have them set aside ex debito justitiae in the exercise of the inherent jurisdiction of the court.
supporting_quote: The proceedings being void, the person affected by them can apply to have them set aside ex debito justitiae in the exercise of the inherent jurisdiction of the court which is saved by S. 839 of the Civil Procedure Code.

statement: An assessor must give reasons in writing for not accepting a return and issuing an assessment.
supporting_quote: Where the Assessor does not accept a return furnished by any person under section 21 for any taxable period and makes an assessment or an additional assessment on such person for such taxable period under section 28 or under section 31, as the case may be, the Assessor shall communicate to such person by registered letter sent through the post why he is not accepting the return.

statement: A Minister's discretion to requisition property under the Cooperative Societies Act should be exercised reasonably, and a failure to derequisition property after a long period of use can be considered unreasonable and subject to a Writ of Mandamus.
supporting_quote: However, if discretion has been used in an unreasonable manner, the said decision is amenable to the Writ jurisdiction.

statement: Administrative authorities must follow a statutory procedure when canceling a lease permit or instrument of disposition.
supporting_quote: An examination of the provisions referred to above would make it clear that before a cancellation of a lease permit or an instrument of disposition, a particular procedure has been clearly laid down in sections 106-128 of the Land Development Ordinance.

statement: An administrative authority cannot act in a manner prejudicial to a person who has a right under the statute to retain the minimum fifty acres under the law.
supporting_quote: The administrative authority cannot act in a manner prejudicial to a person who has a right under the statute to retain the minimum fifty acres under the law.

statement: A nomination made during the pendency of a permit, unless cancelled or revoked, would remain valid and effectual notwithstanding the subsequent issuance of a grant.
supporting_quote: Therefore, a nomination made during the pendency of the permit, unless cancelled or revoked, would remain valid and effectual notwithstanding the subsequent issuance of a grant.

statement: Administrative decisions must be supported by adequate reasons.
supporting_quote: When an administrative body fails to offer satisfactory reasons for its decisions, it risks acting arbitrarily.

statement: The court should consider the intention and the willingness of the original lessee to transfer the land to the successor, and the consent of the original lessee is sufficient even if the other legal heirs do not agree.
supporting_quote: We are of the view that the Court should consider the intention and the willingness of the said Leelawathie which was indicated in several instances to transfer the land to the Petitioner.

statement: A power of attorney must be strictly construed as giving only such authority as it expressly or by necessary implication creates, but this Court cannot decline to recognize the authority that the plaintiff himself has impliedly recognized if the agent has not been objected to.
supporting_quote: a power of attorney must be strictly construed as giving only such authority as it expressly or by necessary implication creates, this Court cannot decline to recognize the authority that the 1st Plaintiff himself has impliedly recognized what Nadarajah Thamilalagan had to do whatever was necessary or ordinarily incidental to the effective execution of an express authority conferred on him by a written document that got onto the record long after the appeal had been preferred to the Civil Appellate High Court of Jaffna.

statement: A person having a claim in respect of a lease at will or for a period not exceeding one month is not a necessary party to a Partition action.
supporting_quote: It was further held that a person having a claim in respect of a lease at will or for a period not exceeding one month, is not a necessary party to a Partition action.

statement: A defendant is entitled to use a road on the basis of necessity if there is no other access road to their property.
supporting_quote: The Defendant-Respondents are entitled to use the disputed road shown as Lot 5 in Plan No 1793 on the basis of necessity.

statement: A cause of action for damages arising from the delict of setting the law in motion is prescribed within 2 years of the arrest.
supporting_quote: Did the Court of Appeal fall into substantial error by completely ignoring the provisions of Section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance? Moreover, in terms of section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance, action for damages should be filed within 2 years of the arrest.

statement: The High Court cannot order a re-trial without specifically setting aside the judgment of the District Court.
supporting_quote: Can the High Court order for re-trial without specifically setting aside the judgment of the District Court? – No.

statement: A co-owner's possession is in law the possession of his co-owners.
supporting_quote: A co-owner’s possession is in law the possession of his co-owners. It is not possible for him to put an end to that possession by any secret intention in his mind. Nothing short of ouster or something equivalent to ouster could bring about the result.

statement: Forfeiture of property used in an offence under the Mines and Minerals Act is discretionary, and the court must hold an inquiry to determine whether the owner had knowledge of the commission of the offence.
supporting_quote: This wording indicates that the court retains judicial discretion in determining whether forfeiture should be ordered.

statement: If the court is satisfied that there are grounds to object to an application, court should frame issues as in Section 533 of the Code and proceed with the matter.
supporting_quote: In the manner issues are framed District Court need to answer same and ensure Justice is done.
